entities.summary:
Caracalla (born Lucius Septimius Bassianus, later Marcus Aurelius Antoninus; 188–217 CE) was Roman emperor from 198 (as co-ruler) and sole emperor from 211 until his assassination in 217. Son of Septimius Severus and Julia Domna, he secured sole power by having his brother Geta murdered in 211 and then conducting a bloody purge of Geta’s supporters. His reign is remembered for military largesse, campaigns in Germany and against Parthia, the Baths of Caracalla in Rome, and above all the Constitutio Antoniniana (212 CE), which extended Roman citizenship to nearly all free inhabitants of the empire.

Ancient historians such as Cassius Dio and Herodian portray him as cruel and erratic; modern scholars also stress fiscal and military pressures that shaped Severan rule. The citizenship edict transformed the legal fabric of the empire, widening the tax base and remaking provincial identity even as Caracalla’s personal tyranny damaged dynastic legitimacy. He was murdered near Carrhae during the eastern campaign, and the Severan system staggered on under Macrinus and later Severan restorations.
